section: GitHub App integration with Pipelines as Code
job_statement: When I need to integrate my Git repositories with OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand how GitHub Apps enable Git-based CI/CD workflows, so I can choose the right integration approach
desired_outcomes: Understand the integration options available
Minimize setup complexity
Ensure secure webhook connectivity
evidence: Lines 78-104: GitHub App integration with Pipelines as Code. Explains that cluster administrators configure a single GitHub App for all users with webhooks pointing to the Pipelines as Code controller.

section: Configure a GitHub App using the command line interface
job_statement: When I need to set up GitHub integration for the main Pipelines as Code controller, I want to use the tkn CLI to create and configure a GitHub App automatically, so I can establish the integration quickly without manual GitHub UI steps
parent_job: Integrate Git repository hosting service with Pipelines as Code
prerequisites: Install tkn command line utility with tkn pac plugin
Log on to OpenShift cluster as cluster administrator
related_jobs: Create GitHub App in administrator perspective
desired_outcomes: Minimize time required to configure GitHub App
Reduce manual configuration errors
Ensure webhook points to correct controller endpoint
evidence: Lines 106-155: Configure a GitHub App using the command line interface. Uses tkn pac bootstrap github-app command to create GitHub App and configure the controller.

section: Create a GitHub App in administrator perspective
job_statement: When I prefer using the web console UI over CLI tools, I want to create and configure a GitHub App through the OpenShift administrator perspective, so I can visually manage the GitHub integration setup
parent_job: Integrate Git repository hosting service with Pipelines as Code
desired_outcomes: Minimize steps required to create GitHub App
Ensure correct permissions are set
Verify app details are saved as secrets
evidence: Lines 157-200: Create a GitHub App in administrator perspective. Uses Pipelines page in admin perspective to setup GitHub App with browser-based workflow.

section: Configure a GitHub App manually and create a secret for Pipelines as Code
job_statement: When I need to configure a GitHub App for additional Pipelines as Code controllers or require full control over the setup, I want to manually create the app in GitHub and configure the OpenShift secret, so I can support multiple GitHub Apps or customize the configuration
parent_job: Integrate Git repository hosting service with Pipelines as Code
prerequisites: Have GitHub account with permissions to create GitHub Apps
Log on to OpenShift cluster as cluster administrator
related_jobs: Configure additional Pipelines as Code controllers
desired_outcomes: Ensure correct repository permissions are set
Minimize risk of exposing webhook secret
Verify private key is securely stored
evidence: Lines 202-310: Configure a GitHub App manually and create a secret for Pipelines as Code. Details manual GitHub App creation with specific permissions and secret configuration for OpenShift.

section: Scope the GitHub token to additional repositories
job_statement: When my pipeline definitions need to access multiple private repositories beyond the main repository, I want to extend the GitHub token scope to additional repositories, so I can fetch tasks and resources from separate private repos
prerequisites: Have Pipelines as Code GitHub App configured
Additional repositories exist in GitHub organization
desired_outcomes: Minimize access token scope while enabling required repository access
Ensure repositories in same namespace can be accessed
Reduce authentication failures when fetching remote tasks
evidence: Lines 312-438: Scope the GitHub token to additional repositories. Explains global and repository-level configuration to extend token scope beyond the pipeline repository.

section: Use Pipelines as Code with GitHub Webhook
job_statement: When I cannot create a GitHub App, I want to use GitHub Webhooks with personal access tokens for Pipelines as Code integration, so I can still trigger pipelines from GitHub events
parent_job: Integrate Git repository hosting service with Pipelines as Code
prerequisites: Install Pipelines as Code on cluster
Create personal access token on GitHub
desired_outcomes: Minimize webhook configuration steps
Ensure secure payload validation
Reduce manual effort in creating Repository CR
evidence: Lines 440-675: Use Pipelines as Code with GitHub Webhook. Provides alternative to GitHub App using webhooks, though without Check Runs API access.

Verify pipeline status reported back to GitLab

section: Use Pipelines as Code with Bitbucket Data Center

section: Configure custom certificates for Pipelines as Code

prerequisites: Install Pipelines as Code using OpenShift Pipelines Operator
desired_outcomes: Ensure Pipelines as Code trusts custom certificates
Minimize TLS verification errors when connecting to Git repositories
Reduce manual certificate distribution
evidence: Lines 1283-1300: Configure custom certificates for Pipelines as Code. Explains using Proxy object to expose custom certificates to all Pipelines components.

section: Private repository support in Pipelines as Code
job_statement: When I need to understand how Pipelines as Code authenticates to private repositories, I want to reference the documentation on git-auth secret management, so I can correctly configure my pipelines to clone private repos
desired_outcomes: Understand automatic secret creation pattern
Minimize authentication errors when cloning private repositories
Ensure git-clone task receives correct credentials
evidence: Lines 1302-1364: Private repository support in Pipelines as Code. Reference material explaining how pac creates git-auth secrets and how to reference them in pipeline/pipelinerun definitions.
